title: Prostate cancer
subtitle: Managed on two axes — extent (localized → PSA-only → metastatic) crossed with castration status (sensitive vs resistant, testosterone <50 ng/dL). Test every metastatic patient for germline + somatic HRR — it now changes therapy in mHSPC as well as mCRPC
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Prostate Cancer (Chien J, Parikh D, Srinivas S) · NCCN · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: Screening & diagnosis
items: USPSTF (Grade C): shared decision on PSA at 55–69; not recommended ≥70. Consider starting at 40–45 for Black men and BRCA2 carriers

Pre-biopsy multiparametric MRI (PI-RADS) → targeted biopsy. PRECISION: clinically significant cancer 38% vs 26% vs standard TRUS biopsy, with fewer insignificant cancers, and 28% of the MRI arm avoided biopsy
Risk inputs: cT stage, Grade Group, PSA, % positive cores, PSA density. Tissue genomic classifiers (Decipher, Prolaris) can refine AS vs treatment
Staging imaging by risk: none for very low / low / favorable intermediate · soft tissue ± bone for unfavorable intermediate · bone + soft tissue for high / very high
PSMA PET (Ga-68 PSMA-11, F-18 piflufolastat) beats CT + bone scan. proPSMA: accuracy 92% vs 65%, fewer equivocal reads. Preferred for BCR restaging and required before Lu-PSMA

blocks.heading: Grade group & NCCN risk (localized)
rows: All of: T1c, GG1, PSA <10, <3 cores positive (≤50% each), PSA density <0.15
cT1–T2a + GG1 + PSA <10, not very low
2–3 IRFs, or GG3, or ≥50% cores positive
blocks.footnote: IRF (intermediate risk factor) = cT2b–T2c, GG2–3, or PSA 10–20. Stage IVA = N1 M0; IVB = M1 (M1a non-regional nodes, M1b bone, M1c other ± bone).

blocks.heading: Localized disease
items: Active surveillance for very low / low and selected favorable intermediate: PSA q6 mo, repeat MRI ± biopsy; treat on upgrading
Definitive: radical prostatectomy or EBRT ± brachytherapy boost — similar cancer control, different toxicity (RP: incontinence, ED; RT: bowel/bladder)
ADT with RT scales with risk: unfavorable intermediate 4–6 mo; high / very high 18–36 mo (~12 mo if brachy boost). Very high or N1: add abiraterone ×2 yr (STAMPEDE)
2026 IPD meta-analysis (13 RCTs, n=10,266): benefit plateaus beyond ~9–12 mo while non-cancer death keeps rising — argues for the short end of each range

boxes: interm./high: RP, or EBRT + ADT 4–6 or 18–36 mo
very high / N1: EBRT + ADT + abiraterone 2 yr
(PEACE-1, ARASENS); low volume: + RT to primary

blocks.heading: Metastatic risk definitions
rows: Visceral mets and/or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1 beyond the spine/pelvis
≥2 of: Gleason ≥8, ≥3 bone lesions, measurable visceral mets
De novo worse than metachronous; favors triplet
blocks.footnote: Volume is judged on CT + bone scan; unvalidated for PSMA-only disease.

blocks.heading: Germline & somatic testing
rows: All metastatic or N1, high/very-high risk, high-risk BCR, Ashkenazi, family history (breast, ovarian, pancreatic, prostate, Lynch); consider if ≤55 or intraductal
Germline DNA-repair mutation 11.8%: BRCA2 5.3%, CHEK2 1.9%, ATM 1.6%, BRCA1 0.9%, regardless of age / family history
HRR panel (tissue or ctDNA) in all metastatic. MSI-H/dMMR + TMB in mCRPC. PTEN IHC (companion test, 2026) in mHSPC
BRCA2 → PARP benefit is largest, and cascade testing of relatives. ATM/CDK12/CHEK2 respond poorly to PARPi

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — evidence by disease state: localized → BCR / nmCRPC → mHSPC → mCRPC

blocks.heading: Localized & high-risk M0 — RT + ADT
rows: RT ± 4 mo ADT, mostly intermediate risk → 10-yr OS 62% vs 57%; benefit confined to intermediate risk
RT ± 3 yr ADT, locally advanced → 10-yr OS 58% vs 40% (HR 0.60)
6 mo vs 3 yr → 6 mo not non-inferior (5-yr OS 81% vs 85%)
Short vs long → long course wins mainly in Gleason 8–10 / high risk (9202 GS 8–10 10-yr OS 45% vs 32%)
18 vs 36 mo, high risk → 10-yr OS 62% vs 62%; 18 mo sufficient, better QoL
13 RCTs → optimal ADT: 0 mo for 1 IRF, 6 mo ≥2 IRFs, 12 mo high risk; gains flatten after ~9–12 mo
High-risk N0 or N1: ADT 3 yr ± abiraterone 2 yr → MFS HR 0.53, 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%, OS HR 0.60. Adding enzalutamide added nothing
Transdermal estradiol vs LHRH, locally advanced M0 → non-inferior MFS (HR 0.96); fractures 5% vs 11%, hot flashes far fewer; gynecomastia 85%

blocks.heading: Biochemical recurrence & nmCRPC
rows: Salvage RT ± bicalutamide 150 mg ×24 mo → 12-yr OS 76% vs 71% (HR 0.77); gynecomastia 70%
Salvage bed RT vs + 4–6 mo ADT vs + ADT + pelvic nodes → 5-yr freedom from progression 71% / 81% / 87%

High-risk BCR (PSADT ≤9 mo): enza + leuprolide vs leuprolide vs enza mono → 5-yr MFS 87% / 71% / 80%. Final OS (2025): combination HR 0.60 (8-yr 79% vs 70%); enzalutamide monotherapy HR 0.83, NOT significant
Post-RP BCR, 52 wk ADT ± apalutamide (± abi) → PSA-PFS 24.9 vs 20.3 mo (HR 0.52); no OS data
nmCRPC, PSADT ≤10 mo: apalutamide → MFS 40.5 vs 16.2 mo; OS 73.9 vs 59.9 (HR 0.78)
Darolutamide → MFS 40.4 vs 18.4 mo; OS HR 0.69 (3-yr 83% vs 77%); least CNS toxicity
blocks.footnote: EMBARK is the reason to use the combination, not enzalutamide alone, when survival is the goal; monotherapy is a compromise for a patient avoiding castration.

blocks.heading: mHSPC — doublet and triplet
rows: ADT ± docetaxel ×6 → OS 57.6 vs 44.0 mo (HR 0.61); benefit concentrated in high volume (49.2 vs 32.2)
+ enzalutamide vs + NSAA (docetaxel allowed) → 3-yr OS 80% vs 72% (HR 0.67)
+ darolutamide (no docetaxel) → rPFS HR 0.54; OS HR 0.81, not significant. FDA June 2025
De novo: ADT ± docetaxel ± abiraterone ± RT → high volume OS 5.1 vs 3.5 yr with abi on top of docetaxel; RT to primary helps low volume
ADT + docetaxel ± darolutamide → OS HR 0.68; little added toxicity
blocks.footnote: Triplet = high-volume, de novo, fit for docetaxel. No trial randomized triplet vs ARPI doublet — the triplet advantage over an ARPI doublet is inferred, not proven.

blocks.heading: mHSPC — biomarker-directed (2025–26)
rows: HRR-altered (56% BRCA): niraparib + AAP vs AAP → rPFS HR 0.52 BRCA, 0.63 ITT. Grade 3–4 AEs 75% vs 59%, anemia 29%. FDA Dec 2025: BRCA2 only
PTEN-deficient by IHC (~25%): capivasertib + AAP → rPFS 33.2 vs 25.7 mo (HR 0.81). Diarrhea 52%, hyperglycemia 38%, rash 35%. FDA June 2026
PSMA PET+: Lu-PSMA ×6 + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI → rPFS HR 0.72. Dry mouth 46%. FDA July 2026
blocks.footnote: All three are rPFS wins with immature or non-significant OS and added toxicity — none yet displaces docetaxel triplet for high-volume disease.

blocks.heading: Choosing mHSPC therapy
items: Low volume or metachronous: ADT + ARPI doublet; add RT to the prostate for low-volume de novo disease
High volume, de novo, fit: triplet — docetaxel + darolutamide (ARASENS) or abiraterone (PEACE-1)

Pick the ARPI by comorbidity: darolutamide for falls, cognition, seizures, polypharmacy; avoid abiraterone with uncontrolled hypertension, diabetes, liver disease; enzalutamide/apalutamide are strong CYP inducers
Then check biomarkers: BRCA2 → niraparib + AAP; PTEN-deficient → capivasertib + AAP; PSMA+ → Lu-PSMA add-on

blocks.heading: mCRPC — PARP inhibitors: trial vs FDA label
rows: Post-ARPI, HRR-selected: olaparib vs ARPI switch → BRCA/ATM rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 (HR 0.34); OS 19.1 vs 14.7
Rucaparib: single-arm BRCA ORR 44% → TRITON3 BRCA rPFS 11.2 vs 6.4 (HR 0.50); ATM no benefit (HR 0.95)
1L, all-comers: olaparib + abiraterone → rPFS HR 0.66 (BRCA 0.23); OS HR 0.81, NS
1L, HRR-selected: niraparib + AAP → BRCA rPFS 16.6 vs 10.9 (HR 0.53); HRR-negative cohort stopped for futility
1L, all-comers: talazoparib + enzalutamide → final OS 45.8 vs 37.0 (HR 0.80); HRR-def OS HR 0.62, BRCA 0.50, non-HRR 0.88 NS
blocks.footnote: Signal tracks BRCA2 > BRCA1 > other HRR; non-HRR benefit is small or absent. PARP + ARPI combinations are for ARPI-naive mCRPC; after an ARPI, use PARP monotherapy.

blocks.heading: mCRPC — radioligand, bone, chemo
rows: PSMA+, post-ARPI + taxane: Lu-PSMA-617 → OS 15.3 vs 11.3 mo (HR 0.62)
Post-ARPI, taxane-naive: Lu-PSMA vs ARPI switch → rPFS 12.0 vs 5.6 (HR 0.41); no OS gain (84% crossover). FDA Mar 2025
Enzalutamide ± Lu-PSMA, 1L mCRPC → OS 34 vs 26 mo (HR 0.55); not approved
Abiraterone + radium → fractures 29% vs 11%, more deaths — unblinded early. Never combine
Enzalutamide + radium, bone agent mandatory → rPFS 19.4 vs 16.4 (HR 0.69); final OS HR 0.76; fractures still 24% vs 13%
Docetaxel q3w OS 18.9 vs 16.5 mo (HR 0.76) · post-docetaxel cabazitaxel 15.1 vs 12.7 (HR 0.70)
Post-docetaxel + 1 ARPI: cabazitaxel vs 2nd ARPI → rPFS 8.0 vs 3.7, OS 13.6 vs 11.0 (HR 0.64)

blocks.heading: mCRPC — sequencing
items: Most patients now reach mCRPC already ARPI-exposed — a second ARPI is the weakest option (CARD)
ARPI-exposed: docetaxel; PARP monotherapy if HRR/BRCA (olaparib, rucaparib); Lu-PSMA if PSMA+ (pre-taxane PSMAfore, post-taxane VISION); then cabazitaxel
ARPI-naive: ARPI, adding a PARPi by genotype — BRCA: olaparib or niraparib + abiraterone; HRR: talazoparib + enzalutamide
Symptomatic bone-only, no visceral disease: radium-223 · MSI-H/dMMR or TMB ≥10: pembrolizumab · asymptomatic, low burden: sipuleucel-T

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, monitoring and key trials

blocks.heading: Hormonal therapy dosing
rows: 3.6 mg SQ q4wk or 10.8 q12wk · 3.75 q4wk / 11.25 q12wk
240 mg SQ load → 80 mg SQ q4wk
360 mg PO load → 120 mg PO daily
Oral antagonist: sustained castration 97% vs 89%, castrate day 4 56% vs 0%, MACE 2.9% vs 6.2%. Adherence matters — T recovers fast
Not licensed for prostate cancer in the US
50 mg daily (flare cover; with ADT) · 150 mg (RTOG 9601)
1000 mg fasting + prednisone 5 mg daily (mHSPC) or 5 mg BID (mCRPC)
Low-dose option: 250 mg with a low-fat meal — non-inferior PSA decline (phase 2) at a quarter of the dose
Steroid switch after abi/pred progression (modest PSA responses)
blocks.footnote: Abiraterone 1000 mg must be taken fasting — food raises exposure several-fold, which is the basis of the low-dose-with-food option.

blocks.heading: Special situations
items: ADT continues indefinitely in CRPC — the AR axis is still active
LHRH agonist flare: if cord/obstructive risk, bicalutamide ~7 days before the agonist, or use an antagonist (castrate by day 3–4)
New metastatic disease with cord compression or impending obstruction: dexamethasone + RT/surgery, and start castration with a GnRH antagonist (degarelix) or orchiectomy — never an agonist alone
Rapid progression with disproportionately low PSA, visceral/lytic mets → suspect neuroendocrine transformation; biopsy, treat with platinum + etoposide
Check testosterone on ADT when PSA rises — not castrate means the ADT is failing, not the cancer

blocks.heading: Chemo, targeted, radioligand dosing
rows: 75 mg/m² q3wk ×6, no prednisone required (CHAARTED; PEACE-1/ARASENS triplet)
75 mg/m² q3wk + prednisone 5 mg BID; 50 mg/m² q2wk if frail
20 mg/m² q3wk (PROSELICA non-inferior) or 25 mg/m² + prednisone; G-CSF prophylaxis
300 mg BID ± abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisone 5 mg BID
200 / 1000 mg fixed-dose tablet daily + prednisone 10 mg (mCRPC) or 5 mg (mCSPC)
400 mg BID, 4 days on / 3 off + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisone
7.4 GBq IV q6wk ×up to 6 — requires PSMA PET positivity
55 kBq/kg IV q4wk ×6 (= the trials' 50 kBq/kg, re-standardized)
3 infusions q2wk — asymptomatic / minimally symptomatic mCRPC

blocks.heading: Bone health & supportive care
items: ADT bone loss: denosumab 60 mg SQ q6 mo or zoledronic acid; calcium + vitamin D
CRPC bone metastases: denosumab 120 mg SQ q4wk or zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q3–4 wk (q12wk acceptable) to prevent skeletal events. No bone agent is indicated for SRE prevention in mHSPC
Before bone agents: dental evaluation (osteonecrosis of the jaw); correct calcium and vitamin D — denosumab causes hypocalcemia; renally dose zoledronic acid
Hot flashes: venlafaxine, gabapentin, or medroxyprogesterone. Exercise (resistance + aerobic) counters fatigue and sarcopenia

blocks.heading: Monitoring & toxicity
items: ADT (all): baseline DEXA, calcium + vitamin D, bone agent if osteoporotic; lipids, A1c, BP (metabolic syndrome, CV risk); hot flashes (venlafaxine, gabapentin); fatigue, sarcopenia → resistance exercise; anemia; cognition

ARPIs: falls and fractures; fatigue; hypertension. Enzalutamide/apalutamide: seizure risk — avoid with seizure history. Apalutamide: rash, TSH. Check drug interactions (enza/apa are strong inducers — DOACs, statins, immunosuppressants)
Abiraterone: mineralocorticoid excess — hypokalemia, hypertension, edema; LFTs q2wk ×3 mo then monthly; take 1000 mg on an empty stomach
PARPi: anemia (talazoparib grade ≥3 43–49%) — CBC monthly, transfuse / dose-reduce; MDS/AML rare; VTE with olaparib + abiraterone (7% vs 2%)
Lu-PSMA: xerostomia (~45%), nausea, fatigue, cytopenias (CBC before each dose), renal function
Radium-223: ANC ≥1.5, platelets ≥100 before first dose; not with abiraterone; bone agent if combined with enzalutamide
Capivasertib: diarrhea, hyperglycemia (fasting glucose/A1c), rash
Taxanes: neutropenia, neuropathy (docetaxel), diarrhea (cabazitaxel)

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Enza + leuprolide in high-risk BCR — MFS and OS HR 0.60; monotherapy no OS gain
Docetaxel (high volume) / abiraterone (high risk) with ADT in mHSPC
ARPI in nmCRPC — MFS ~2 yr longer, OS HR 0.69–0.78
Talazoparib + enza 1L mCRPC — OS HR 0.80; label HRR-only
Cabazitaxel beats a second ARPI — OS HR 0.64
Radium + abiraterone harms; + enzalutamide helps with bone protection
Oral relugolix vs leuprolide — better castration, fewer MACE

Exercise (resistance + aerobic) counters fatigue and sarcopenia Monitoring & toxicity ADT (all): baseline DEXA , calcium + vitamin D, bone agent if osteoporotic; lipids, A1c, BP (metabolic syndrome, CV risk); hot flashes (venlafaxine, gabapentin); fatigue, sarcopenia → resistance exercise; anemia; cognition ARPIs: falls and fractures ; fatigue; hypertension. Enzalutamide/apalutamide: seizure risk — avoid with seizure history. Apalutamide: rash, TSH.
